Exodus chapter 24:4 says that when Moses was going to build an altar, he rose up early in the morning. There is a divine appointment that God schedules in the morning. Psalm 5:3 says, "My voice shall thou hear in the morning, O Lord. In the morning will I direct my prayer unto thee and will look up." Psalm 59:16 says, "But I will sing of thy power in the morning." Psalm 63:1 says, "O God, thou art my God. Early will I seek thee." The pattern is consistent throughout scripture. Those who encountered God, those who received miracles, those who saw breakthroughs, they were morning people. Let me tell you why the morning is so strategic. Number one, the morning is when mercy is distributed. Lamentations chapter 3 verses 22 to 23 says, "It is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed because his compassions fail not. >> [music] >> They are new every morning. Great is thy faithfulness." Every morning God releases fresh mercy. Every morning God distributes new compassion. Every morning there is a divine allocation of grace. [music] But here is the question, if mercy is being distributed in the morning, where are you when distribution is happening? If you are in bed when grace is being distributed, [music] you might be overlooked. The early bird catches the worm. The morning seeker receives the blessing. The early riser catches the anointing. Number two, the morning is when battles are won. 2 Chronicles chapter 20 verse 20 says, "And they rose early in the morning and went forth into the wilderness of Tekoa." This was the day Jehoshaphat and Judah defeated their enemies without lifting a sword. They rose early. They didn't wait until afternoon. They didn't wait until they felt like it. They rose early. When you rise early to pray, you are not being religious, you are being strategic. You are positioning yourself for victory before the battle begins. The enemy doesn't want you to pray in the morning because he knows that if you capture the morning, you will win the day. Number three, the morning is when direction is revealed. Exodus chapter 16 verse 7 says, "And in the morning, then you shall see the glory of the Lord. In the morning, you shall see. Not in the afternoon, not in the evening. In the morning. If you need direction, pray in the morning. If you need clarity, seek God in the morning. If you need guidance, meet with heaven in the morning. Number four, the morning is when resurrection power is released. Mark chapter 16 verse 9 says, "Now when Jesus was risen early the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene." Jesus rose in the morning. Resurrection happened in the morning. New life was released in the morning. When you pray in the morning, you are tapping into resurrection power. When you seek God at daybreak, you are accessing the same power that raised Jesus from the dead. When you worship at sunrise, you are connecting with the God of new beginnings. Hallelujah.
